commands.short: Login via OAuth2 PKCE (auto browser → --manual fallback)
commands.long:
Authenticate with Gate using OAuth2 PKCE and an Agentic subaccount.

The browser selects or creates the subaccount and confirms the granted permissions.
By default all six permissions are requested; --scope requests an explicit subset.
Use --manual to copy the authorization URL into a browser and paste the code here.
Use --force to register a new client and authorize again. Existing credentials are
retained until a new result is saved. A cancelled login keeps the old local state.

Examples:
  gate-cli cex auth login
  gate-cli cex auth login --manual --scope base,stock
  gate-cli cex auth login --force

flags.name: force
flags.usage: Register a new client and re-authorize; retain old credentials until success

flags.usage: Manual mode: copy URL to browser, paste code back

commands.short: Refresh the bound OAuth2 token once
commands.exclusion: Shared authentication

commands.short: Show current OAuth2 status (run this FIRST before login)
commands.long:
Print the OAuth2 token status for the fixed production OAuth issuer.

Output states:
  authenticated          Locally unexpired; remote grant may have been revoked.
  expired (refreshable)  Will auto-refresh on the next API call.
  expired                Re-login required (refresh token absent/expired).
  Not logged in          No token stored; run 'gate-cli cex auth login'.

AGENT GUIDANCE:
  This is the recommended entry point when deciding whether authentication
  is needed. Run 'status' first; only invoke 'login' if the output is
  "Not logged in" or "expired" (non-refreshable). This avoids redundant
  browser launches and unnecessary prompts to the user.

Related:
  gate-cli cex auth login   — authorize (auto browser, --manual fallback)
  gate-cli cex auth logout  — clear stored tokens
